title: Local dichotomy for a pure subcurve at a smooth point or a split node
statement: Let X be a reduced finite-type curve over a field k and i:Y→X a reduced pure one-dimensional closed subcurve, all components of X also of dimension one [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let y be closed in Y. Suppose X is smooth at i(y), or its residue field there is finite separable over k and its completed stalk is isomorphic to κ(i(y))[[u,v]]/(uv) [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Put Z equal to the scheme-theoretic complementary closure and T=Y×_X Z [def-pc-fibre-product]. Either the stalk map O_X→O_Y is an isomorphism, ambient smoothness implies subcurve smoothness, and i(y) is outside Z; or X is nonsmooth there, Y is smooth at y, and every T stalk over y is a field.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: At a smooth ambient point take a smooth neighbourhood and a connected-component open neighbourhood. Its stalks are regular local domains, so this connected locally Noetherian neighbourhood is irreducible. The complementary-component theorem shows that its range is contained in Y. The restricted closed immersion is surjective onto a reduced scheme, hence an isomorphism. This gives the stalk isomorphism and smoothness; the neighbourhood misses the closure of the complementary open.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: At a nonsmooth point lying in Z, apply the boundary-local-rings theorem. Closed immersions induce isomorphisms of residue fields, respecting k, so separability transfers to κ(y). The regular-separable-residue criterion gives a smooth Y-neighbourhood; retain the field-stalk conclusion for T.

source.place: Tag 0E38, proof of lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve, split-node specialization.

proof.text: Outside Z, its open complement is contained in the range of Y, since the complementary open is contained in its closure. The restricted closed immersion is surjective onto this reduced open scheme, hence an isomorphism. This gives the first alternative also at an ambient node.

lean.statement:
theorem split_nodal_subcurve_local_dichotomy
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, topologicalKrullDim C = 1)
    (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsReduced Y]
    (hY : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents Y, topologicalKrullDim C = 1)
    (y : Y) (hy : IsClosed ({y} : Set Y))
    (hlocal : (∃ U : X.Opens, i y ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f)) ∨
      ((f.residueFieldAlgebraMap (i y)).Finite ∧
        @Algebra.IsSeparable k (X.residueField (i y)) _ _
          (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap (i y)).toAlgebra ∧
        Nonempty (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk (i y)))
          (X.presheaf.stalk (i y)) ≃+*
          (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) (X.residueField (i y)) ⧸
            Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2)
              (X.residueField (i y))) * MvPowerSeries.X 1})))) :
    (IsIso (i.stalkMap y) ∧
      ((∃ U : X.Opens, i y ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f)) →
        ∃ U : Y.Opens, y ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ i ≫ f)) ∧
      i y ∉ Set.range (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι) ∨
    ((¬ ∃ U : X.Opens, i y ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f)) ∧
      (∃ U : Y.Opens, y ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ i ≫ f)) ∧
      ∀ t : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) i
          (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι,
        pullback.fst i (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι t = y →
        IsField ((pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) i
          (Scheme.openComplementOfIsClosedImmersion i).ι.imageι).presheaf.stalk t))
